title: SECTION VI — QUESTIONS
summary: A concentrated sequence organised around questions rather than final answers. It revisits major problems of Indian philosophy—Śruti, sūtra, witness and prakṛti, karma, pramāṇa, one and many, suffering, society, language and liberation—while also opening toward comparison. The poems treat philosophical traditions as living fields of dispute whose differences should remain visible.

entries.title: The Question Flowing Behind the Fixed Image
entries.summary: A meditation on knowledge & reason, body & consciousness and earth & natural imagery. The recurring register of body and breath helps carry the poem’s movement. Close reading (PDF p. 497; printed p. 496): The fixed image under scrutiny is an account of Indian philosophy that allows only spirituality, immobility or withdrawal. Such a portrait hides the arguments and material questions that complicate it. The poem asks for renewed attention to that internal variety. Its intervention concerns the method of reading as much as the conclusion: a tradition cannot answer back if the reader has already decided which kinds of question it is permitted to contain.

entries.title: The Sky of Thought Beyond the Axis of Liberation
entries.summary: A meditation on knowledge & reason, freedom & liberation and earth & natural imagery. The recurring register of sky and light imagery helps carry the poem’s movement. Close reading (PDF p. 498; printed p. 497): The desire for liberation does not have to become the organising purpose of every inquiry. Knowing can have an interest of its own, even where practical and spiritual goals remain important. The poem distinguishes these motivations without requiring their total separation. That distinction gives philosophy room to ask questions whose answers do not immediately supply a programme of release. Intellectual variety depends on allowing more than one reason to think.

entries.title: Liberation Is One Question, Thought Has Many Paths
entries.summary: A meditation on knowledge & reason, freedom & liberation and language & meaning. The recurring register of sky and light imagery helps carry the poem’s movement. Close reading (PDF p. 499; printed p. 498): The poem complicates the word liberation before allowing it to settle an argument. Different accounts of release need not name the same condition, and a metaphysical explanation does not automatically establish an ethical goal. The plurality of paths therefore requires more than a generous assertion that all positions agree. The reader must ask what each position means, what problem it answers and which commitments would follow from accepting it.

entries.title: In the Forest of Shruti, Whose Voice Is Original?
entries.summary: A meditation on earth & natural imagery, time & impermanence and knowledge & reason. It moves from earth & natural imagery toward time & impermanence, allowing the poem’s emphasis to change as it develops. Close reading (PDF p. 500; printed p. 499): The forest image directs attention to layered voices rather than a single, transparent speaker. Ritual settings, modes of instruction and different textual emphases complicate an appeal to original authority. Selection is part of how an inheritance reaches its reader. The poem makes that process visible and asks whose voice becomes representative. Preserving difference within the tradition is a condition of understanding it, not simply an obstacle to a tidy account.
